goal: Make Bronze usable as a local queue in tauri dev: wire dead-but-specified composer, list, copy, settings, permissions, library search, and Rust-owned backup/export/import; replace parchment/bronze-brown tokens with a clean zinc system; default hand-test locale to en with real spaces and no mid-word smash.
outcome: In pnpm --filter desktop tauri dev, Library/Settings/Help open real Tauri windows; composer Add persists and the list mutates via existing domain/storage; Copy uses the 6-4 pasteboard path; Settings load/save SettingsV1 and permission Retest/Open System Settings work from the Settings window; library search is substring-only with QUE_007_COMPLETE=false and ADR-018 Proposed; backup/export/import use a Rust picker (no WebView paths); surfaces share a near-white zinc palette with one cool accent and body contrast >=4.5:1; UI locale is en unless explicitly requested; AX capture is not faked; seeded shortcuts stay disabled; human 3.9/3.10/5.5/9.3 stay backlog.

requirements.statement: Never accept ADR-002, ADR-009, or ADR-018 silently; leave them Proposed.
Do not copy Cooper source or Copper trade dress, name, icons, or pixel-identical chrome.
Event-tap callbacks must not touch AX, DB, windows, clipboard, or logging.
No network, telemetry, accounts, remote fonts, CDN, hosted AI, or analytics.
Every user-facing string belongs in the locale catalog; no sentence concatenation.
Never accept arbitrary filesystem paths from WebView; pickers stay Rust-owned.
Do not fake a full capture event-tap from JavaScript; composer is the working add path if AX is unfinished.
Do not invent a new shortcut system; leave seeded registry disabled unless enabling documented 7-2 defaults.
Work only on branch bmad/bronze-autonomous; never push.
Do not invent a Swift verify command; pnpm verify is the repo bar.
Given tauri dev, when the user adds an item from the composer, then it persists and appears in the queue list.
Given Settings, when locale is default, then strings are English with real spaces and permission cards remain readable at the default window width.
Given the four HTML surfaces, when styled, then they share a zinc/neutral palette without #8c6239 or #f7f4ef brand brown.
